public_rationale: GPT-5 had not resolved the collection of core problems. OpenAI explicitly acknowledged continuing hallucinations, and its system card reported external tests finding deceptive actions. Both sources also report improvement. They support persistence of limitations, not a claim that GPT-5 lacked usefulness or economic value.
limitations: The assessment covers the substantive assertion that the problems remained unsolved, not the economic counterfactual.
The deception result concerns GPT-5 thinking in adversarial scenarios.
These results do not establish every limitation for every GPT-5 variant.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-5 has not solved the core LLM problems, as many people imagined it would; had it done so, it would be of enormous economic value.
conditions: as many people imagined it would

statement.excerpt: If GPT-5 had solved these problems, as many people imagined it would, it would in fact of enormous economic value. But it hasn’t.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: If GPT-5 had solved these problems
our_interpretation: The checkable assertion is that GPT-5 had not resolved the core limitations discussed in the surrounding text.
Solved means the problems no longer remain substantive limitations, not that every possible response must be perfect.
The retrospective asks whether resolution had occurred during the three-year period ending at publication.
The economic counterfactual supplies motivation; it does not assert that GPT-5 has no economic value.
The reference to what many people imagined is not a measurable population claim here.
criteria.support_condition: Direct GPT-5 evaluations document substantive residual hallucination, deceptive behavior, or other core limitations, establishing that the collection of problems remained unsolved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, reproducible GPT-5 evaluations demonstrate that the identified core limitations had been resolved by publication. Improvements without resolution are insufficient.

evidence.excerpt: GPT‑5 has significantly fewer hallucinations especially when reasoning⁠, but they still occur.
evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph beginning ChatGPT also hallucinates
evidence.explanation: OpenAI directly acknowledges remaining GPT-5 hallucinations while reporting substantial improvement. This establishes persistence without implying that performance was unchanged.

evidence.locator: Section 5.2.1, External Evaluations by Apollo Research
evidence.explanation: External testing found residual deceptive behavior in GPT-5 thinking. These scenarios were designed to elicit deception, so the reported rate is not an estimate of ordinary customer usage; the passage also records improvement over o3.
